sources.title: UK local authority and regional greenhouse gas emissions statistics, 2005 to 2024
2005 to 2024 UK local and regional greenhouse gas emissions technical report (web accessible)

guard_patterns.handling: Keep the published local-authority scope and exclusions.
Keep end-user, activity, spatial and gas bases explicit.
Allow annual inventory revisions; do not freeze historical estimates.
Do not convert LA/statistical allocations to site or parcel measurements.
Never infer a parcel emission value from these statistics.
Require explicit PASS review for each generated control.

packages.title: 2026 local GHG inventory boundary and end-user basis QA
facts: Estimates cover the 2005-2024 period and provide a nationally consistent sub-national evidence base.
The dataset spatially disaggregates territorial CO2, CH4 and N2O emissions from the UK GHG Inventory.
Fluorinated gases are not included in the local dataset because suitable local allocation data are unavailable.
Aviation, shipping and military transport emissions without an obvious local allocation basis are excluded from the local-area statistics.
The dataset is presented on an end-user basis rather than simply where energy-production emissions physically occur.
Fuel-production and electricity-production emissions are reallocated to users of those fuels on the end-user basis.
National end-user emissions are used to derive emission factors for activities.
Local-authority activity data are multiplied by relevant emission factors to estimate local emissions.
Large sources can use more detailed site-specific emissions and fuel-consumption information than national allocation methods.
The local dataset and the UK GHG Inventory are subject to continuous methodological improvement.

packages.title: 2026 local GHG coverage and exclusions QA
facts: The local and regional statistics cover territorial CO2, CH4 and N2O.
Fluorinated gases remain outside the local-area estimates.
National inventory emissions from aviation are not allocated to local areas when there is no obvious allocation basis.
National inventory emissions from shipping are not allocated to local areas when there is no obvious allocation basis.
Military transport emissions are not allocated to local areas where no obvious local basis exists.
The main source datasets include the UK National Atmospheric Emissions Inventory and DESNZ sub-national energy statistics.
The statistics use nationally available datasets to support consistency across local authorities.
The estimates are intended to support local and regional indicators and emissions-reduction planning.
The statistics alone are not sufficient to monitor every local emissions-reduction initiative.
Local supplementary monitoring may still be needed for initiatives not resolved by national datasets.

packages.title: 2026 non-domestic electricity allocation QA
facts: NAEI end-user electricity GHG emissions are distributed across local authorities in proportion to electricity consumption.
Electricity emissions in this dataset are around 97% CO2 each year.
Electricity profile classes 1 and 2 identify domestic customers while profile classes 3 to 8 identify non-domestic customers.
Profile 1 and 2 meters above 100,000 kWh annual consumption are reallocated to the non-domestic sector.
Profile 1 and 2 meters above 50,000 kWh can be reallocated where address information indicates non-domestic use.
Unallocated electricity consumption is retained where accurate local georeferencing is not possible.
In 2024 the non-domestic electricity unallocated share was reported as 6.1%.
In 2024 the domestic electricity unallocated share was reported as 0.06%.
Non-domestic electricity is split into Industry, Agriculture, Commercial and Public Sector categories using SIC07 groupings.
Except for large point sources, employment and energy-use proxies are used where consistent site-level energy data are unavailable.

packages.title: 2026 non-domestic gas AQ period and classification QA
facts: DESNZ sub-national gas statistics provide domestic and non-domestic gas consumption estimates for Great Britain local authorities for 2005-2024.
Gas data are based on information from Xoserve and independent gas transporters.
Gas meter locations are mapped to local authorities using the National Statistics Postcode Directory.
Annual Quantity gas consumption is an annualised estimate based on meter readings at least six months apart.
The gas consumption period was 1 October to 30 September for 2005-2015.
The period shifted during 2016 and 2017 because of changes in data collection.
From 2018 onward the period is approximately mid-May to mid-May.
Previous-year Annual Quantity values can be carried forward when new meter readings are unavailable.
Weather correction is applied to AQ data except at sites with automatic meter reading.
The 73,200 kWh industry cut-off can misclassify small businesses as domestic and some larger domestic users as non-domestic.

packages.title: 2026 large industrial point-source mapping QA
facts: Large industrial installations are mapped using NAEI point-source data.
An additional end-user calculation accounts for emissions from processing fuels used at industrial installations.
Site-specific estimates combine detailed fuel-consumption and emissions datasets.
Installation data include records from regulators for sites in the UK ETS or historically the EU ETS.
Large point sources are treated separately from area-source proxy mapping where site-specific information is available.
Some very large gas-consumer data are suppressed in published consumption statistics to maintain confidentiality.
Suppressed large gas consumers are represented within the large-industrial-installations sector.
Point-source location information is considered comparatively strong for large industrial installations.
ETS installation emissions are reported and verified, although monitoring quality can still vary.
Non-ETS large industrial sources can retain modelled components and therefore higher uncertainty than ETS point sources.

packages.title: 2026 non-domestic other employment mapping QA
facts: Industrial sectors are mapped using a combination of point-source estimates and employment-based area-source distributions.
Some sectors are fully represented by identified point sources.
Other sectors have no identified point sources and are mapped entirely as area sources.
Employment is used as a proxy where site-specific fuel use is unavailable.
Heavy-industry employment distributions are used for some industrial off-road emission mapping.
Non-domestic electricity and gas category splits use employment and energy-use information outside large point sources.
Industry, agriculture, commercial and public-sector electricity categories are derived from SIC07 groupings.
For 2015 onward, category splits are specific to local authority and year.
For 2005-2014, the 2015 split is applied where the newer employment-based method is used.
Employment-based distributions introduce spatial uncertainty because local energy intensity can differ from model assumptions.

packages.title: 2026 agricultural emissions spatial-model QA
facts: Agricultural emissions estimates account for management practices in the national inventory.
Management-practice assumptions are applied at country level rather than local-authority level.
The agricultural model was jointly developed by Rothamsted Research, ADAS, UKCEH and Cranfield University.
The model was first implemented for the 2016 inventory.
Model outputs include 10 km by 10 km agricultural emissions estimates.
Those estimates are spatially resolved to non-disclosive 1 km by 1 km emission maps.
Agriculture includes important methane and nitrous oxide sources.
Methane and nitrous oxide emissions are generally more uncertain than carbon dioxide because processes depend strongly on environmental and management factors.
Local agricultural estimates should not be interpreted as direct farm-level measurements.
Annual inventory improvements can revise the agricultural time series.

packages.title: 2026 domestic electricity and gas boundary QA
facts: Domestic electricity consumption is identified primarily from profile classes 1 and 2 subject to non-domestic reclassification rules.
Domestic electricity emissions are allocated using sub-national electricity consumption data.
Domestic gas estimates use DESNZ local-authority gas consumption statistics.
Great Britain domestic gas data cover 2005-2024.
Northern Ireland domestic gas local estimates are available for 2015-2024 in the referenced DESNZ source.
Domestic gas emissions include CO2, CH4 and N2O calculated using implied emission factors.
Sub-national gas consumption does not exactly match DUKES because the datasets use different aggregation and time bases.
Gas-year timing means a local-statistics year can represent consumption spanning parts of two calendar years.
The 73,200 kWh classification threshold can place some small businesses in the domestic category.
Domestic energy estimates are statistical allocations and should not be treated as parcel or household measurements.

packages.title: 2026 road transport COPERT and end-user factors QA
facts: Road transport fuel-consumption factors are derived from COPERT 5 fuel-consumption-speed relationships.
COPERT is a vehicle-emissions model and factor database used for road-transport emissions estimation.
Petrol and diesel factors incorporate biofuel content within weighted fuel factors rather than modelling those biofuel fractions separately.
Local-authority road factors are derived from NAEI by-source emission factors.
Road factors are adjusted to an end-user basis to include fuel-production and processing emissions.
CO2 factors per unit fuel differ between petrol and diesel.
NAEI CO2 factors per unit fuel do not vary by vehicle type in this local-authority calculation.
CH4 and N2O factors do vary by vehicle as well as fuel type.
The technical report publishes annual by-source and end-user factors through 2024.
Method and input-data revisions can change the historical road-transport time series.

packages.title: 2026 road-network and speed mapping QA
facts: The Great Britain hot-exhaust road network base uses Ordnance Survey Open Roads data.
Northern Ireland road mapping uses a Land and Property Services road dataset.
Fuel-consumption factors for each road depend on urban status, road type and speed limit.
Major-road speed limits are taken from a dedicated speed-limit dataset.
Minor-road speed limits are assumed to be 30 mph in urban areas and 60 mph in rural areas.
Road-network factors are combined with national road-traffic data.
Traffic count data are used to distribute activity on major roads.
Average flows and speeds do not capture all within-day and within-year variation.
Minor-road activity relies more heavily on regional average flows and vehicle splits.
Road-emissions mapping therefore carries higher spatial uncertainty on minor roads than on major count-point networks.

packages.title: 2026 other-transport and rail allocation QA
facts: Other transport includes road LPG, road natural gas, lubricants, urea, railway coal, inland waterways and aircraft support vehicles.
These other-transport sources are distributed using detailed NAEI spatial maps.
Electricity used by railways cannot be cleanly separated from other commercial and industrial electricity in the DESNZ dataset.
Rail electricity emissions are therefore included within commercial and industrial sectors rather than a separate rail electricity sub-sector.
Diesel and coal railway emissions are represented in separate transport sub-sectors.
Road LPG and natural-gas combustion use fuel-consumption-factor methods consistent with the road-transport approach.
Combustion of lubricants is allocated using total vehicle-kilometre estimates from traffic-flow maps.
Other-transport spatial allocations can be less certain when precise locations of fuel use are unavailable.
The local dataset excludes national shipping emissions where no obvious local allocation basis exists, while locally allocable domestic-navigation sources can be represented.
Other-transport outputs are geographic estimates, not journey-level or vehicle-level measurements.

packages.title: 2026 LULUCF source-sink and mapping QA
facts: LULUCF activities can be both sources and sinks of atmospheric carbon dioxide.
LULUCF also produces methane and nitrous oxide emissions.
Land conversion to cropland and settlements generally produces emissions.
Forest growth and conversion of cropland to grassland can remove carbon dioxide.
UK LULUCF is described as a net CO2 sink in the technical report.
When CH4 and N2O are included, the report states LULUCF becomes a net source on a CO2e basis.
Peatland condition, drainage ditches, wildfire and land conversion are among mapped LULUCF emission processes.
Nitrogen fertilisation of new forests and soil mineralisation after land-use change can generate N2O.
UKCEH supplies regional LULUCF data under the NAEI programme.
A separate 2026 mapping report provides the detailed local-authority LULUCF disaggregation methodology and recalculation context.

packages.title: 2026 landfill waste-origin reallocation QA
facts: The local-authority dataset uniquely reallocates landfill emissions back to the producer location of the waste.
Solid-waste disposal is a key methane category in the UK greenhouse-gas inventory.
Landfill methane arises from decomposition of biodegradable solid waste.
Country-level landfill methane totals come from the national inventory.
Local allocation uses landfill-origin data from UK environmental regulators and administrations.
The biological fraction of each waste type is applied to derive biodegradable mass by local authority.
Country methane totals are apportioned using the mass of biological waste originating in each local authority.
England waste-data-interrogator records are available from 2006, with the 2005 split based on 2006.
Where only a region of origin is known, waste is split among local authorities using ONS population data for that year.
This top-down local allocation can differ from bottom-up waste-emission calculations using company-reporting conversion factors.

packages.title: 2026 other-waste process mapping QA
facts: Non-electricity waste-process emissions for 2018-2020 entered the local dataset from the 2020 submission.
A full non-electricity waste-process time series back to 2005 has been included since the 2022 submission.
Electricity used by the waste industry is accounted for under non-domestic electricity.
Electricity-related emissions from energy-from-waste plants are associated with the end user of the electricity.
Wastewater-treatment emissions are included in other waste.
Sewage-sludge decomposition emissions are included in other waste.
Composting emissions are included in other waste.
Anaerobic-digestion emissions are included in other waste.
Other-waste emissions are mapped in part using ONS population statistics.
Recent inventory revisions materially affected wastewater and landfill estimates, so historic local values can be recalculated.

packages.title: 2026 local GHG uncertainty-method QA
facts: National inventory uncertainty is calculated using Monte Carlo simulation.
Probability distributions are assigned to emission factors and activity data in the national uncertainty analysis.
Local-statistics sectors do not exactly match the UK National Inventory Document sectors.
National percentage-error estimates are combined using emission-weighted averages to align them to local-statistics sectors.
Geographical-distribution uncertainty is difficult to quantify directly.
Except for DESNZ gas and electricity data, quantitative uncertainty estimates for individual spatial components are generally unavailable.
Mapping uncertainties therefore use expert judgement and expert elicitation informed by IPCC guidance.
Gas and electricity mapping uncertainty estimates include meter-location allocation quality.
Local-authority total uncertainty combines national emission uncertainty and mapping uncertainty using a sum-of-squares method.
LULUCF uncertainty is excluded from the main combined local-authority uncertainty analysis because it can dominate and mask other sector variation.
